newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Upbeat outlook for Germany's RWE.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Upbeat outlook for Germany's RWE.

text.p: German diversified utility giant RWE AG said on Friday it expected a 6.8 percent rise in group net profit in the first nine months of its 1996/97 business year to continue for the full year to end of June.
In the nine months to March 31, RWE increased its group net profit to 878 million marks ($515.2 million) from 822 million marks in the year-earlier period, a rise of 6.8 percent.

"The (earnings) growth will continue. Earnings growth was mostly seen in the energy, engineering and plant construction sectors, while investments in the telecommunications business are clearly higher, as expected," RWE said in a statement.
Lynn Reinhardt, utilities analyst with BZW Bank in Frankfurt, said: "These figures are bang in line with our expectations."
"We have forecast an earnings per share growth of 6.5 percent over the year and this is also more or less in line with the company's own projections," she said.

Group sales rose 7.8 percent to 52.9 billion marks from 49.1 billion, the company said. Sales fell slightly in the group's energy business, down around 1.5 percent to 16.226 billion marks in the nine months to the end of March.
At the same time RWE said it was able to improve the competitiveness of this sector, mainly due to lower energy prices since January.
Sales in RWE's mining and minerals division fell 16.1 percent to 3.032 billion marks.

The biggest turnover gains were in the group's fledgling telecommunications business, which saw sales grow 115.2 percent to 812 million marks. The sales increase mainly came from the telecoms service provision business of the telecoms unit.

The highlights of the group's acquisitions were its purchase of 20 percent of Motor Columbus and 79 percent of printing equipment maker Linotype-Hell, which it acquired via its Heidelberger Druck unit.

For the whole financial year, the main feature of the group's investment policy would be its investment in telecommunications and it said its telecommunications joint venture with fellow diversified utility Veba AG, called o.tel.o, had started operations.
When RWE entered the joint venture in the autumn of last year it said it would pay a total of around 3.6 billion marks into the venture.

"Within the framework of our joint-venture agreement, we will be making a payment of 2.2 billion marks towards the joint venture. We will pay for this out of current cash-flow and current group liquidity," said RWE in a statement.
RWE had previously quit a telecoms alliance with Viag AG and British Telecom.

The group said the number of employees at the group had increased slightly in the early part of the year, but net of first-time consolidations staff actually fell by 4.5 percent in the first nine months of the year.
The average number of employees in the first nine months was 132,711 people, down from 135,964.

Traders on the German stock exchange were underwhelmed by the news, and shares in RWE ended the bourse session down 25 pfennigs at 73.35 marks, underperforming the overall market which was up slightly at 3,556.75 points.
Market sentiment was somewhat muted by the fact that many market players took Friday off after Thursday's Ascension Day holiday.
